Sensitivity Analysis for the Pennsylvania Reemployment Bonus Experiment

Source: vignettes/bonus.Rmd
bonus.Rmd

Introduction

In this vignette, we demonstrate sensitivity analysis for debiased machine learning using the Pennsylvania Reemployment Bonus experiment data. The experiment randomly assigned unemployment insurance (UI) claimants to a treatment group that received a cash bonus for finding employment quickly.

The main question is: does the reemployment bonus reduce unemployment duration?

Load Data 

# loads package
library(dml.sensemakr)

# loads data
data("Penn")

# outcome: log unemployment duration
y <- Penn[, "inuidur1"]

# treatment: assignment to bonus group
d <- Penn[, "tg"]

# covariates
x <- model.matrix(~ -1 + female + black + othrace + dep +
                     q2 + q3 + q4 + q5 + q6 +
                     agelt35 + agegt54 +
                     durable + lusd + husd, data = Penn)

Partially Linear Model

We estimate the average treatment effect (ATE) of the reemployment bonus on log unemployment duration using the partially linear model (PLM) with random forests (the default).

# run DML (partially linear model)
dml.bonus <- dml(y, d, x, model = "plm", cf.folds = 5, cf.reps = 5)

# results under conditional ignorability
summary(dml.bonus)

Sensitivity Analysis

Even though the treatment was randomized, we can still examine how robust these results are to potential violations of the identification assumptions.

# sensitivity analysis
sens.bonus <- sensemakr(dml.bonus, cf.y = 0.03, cf.d = 0.03)

# summary
summary(sens.bonus)

Contour Plots

The contour plots show how the confidence bounds change as a function of the sensitivity parameters cf.y (confounding with the outcome) and cf.d (confounding with the treatment).

# contour plots
oldpar <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(sens.bonus, which.bound = "lwr", bound.label = "Scenario")
plot(sens.bonus, which.bound = "upr", bound.label = "Scenario")
par(oldpar)

Interpretation

The robustness values indicate the minimum strength of association that omitted variables would need to have with both the outcome and the treatment in order to change the qualitative conclusions of the study. Higher robustness values indicate more robust findings.
